display.title: Episode 190: Saved by a Miracle, Chapter 1 (Elul)
display.summary_short: An Elul show: why we check our tefillin and mezuzos this month, Shema with a five-year-old guest, and chapter 1 of a story about an honest Chassid falsely accused.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the month of Elul 5745. Uncle Yossi explains that Elul is the time to end the year well, and that is why we have our tefillin and mezuzos checked by a trained sofer: letters can fade or crack in a hot, dry spot, and wet paint can seep into the case. A mezuzah is like a guard at the door, a sign that Hashem is welcome in the house. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, a five-year-old guest who came from Eretz Yisroel leads the Shema. Story time begins 'Through the Eyes of a Tzaddik' (catalogued as 'Saved by a Miracle'). Reb Baruch, an honest and well-liked supervisor in a government lumberyard, is envied by the cruel Alex, who hides twenty stolen logs in Reb Baruch's barn and denounces him to the minister. Reb Baruch is summoned to appear on Tuesday morning and hurries to the Alter Rebbe, who smiles and tells him to come back next week. Trusting the tzaddik, Reb Baruch decides not to go. The show closes with a call to sign up friends for Tzivos Hashem and a reminder about Dial-a-Jewish-Story.
display.lesson: Trust Hashem and the guidance of a tzaddik even when you cannot understand it; and in Elul, make sure your mitzvos, like tefillin and mezuzos, are in the best shape.
